page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, powered by a 2.5 GHz 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, accompanied by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 4.0 GB total, delivering 2.0 GB per vCPU, and network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps without bundled public IPv4 addresses.

A key component of the c6gd.large configuration is the bundled local storage, featuring a direct-attached 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. This local storage delivers high-speed input/output operations suitable for temporary scratch space, ephemeral caching, and transient file manipulation without relying exclusively on networked block storage. The system does not include dedicated graphics processing units, confining compute tasks strictly to the ARM CPU cores.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the entry-level footprint of the 2-core Graviton2 silicon. While stress-ng single-core performance registers in the average tier at 1519.49, multi-core throughput drops into lower deciles with a score of 3013.99. Memory bandwidth reaches 36.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 18.33 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific tests reveal Redis SET throughput at 2.35 million operations per second, static web serving at 2.32 GB/sec, and Clang compilation at a Geekbench sub-score of 2272.0.

Given its 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio and bundled NVMe drive, the c6gd.large is best suited for lightweight compute workloads requiring rapid ephemeral disk access, including CI/CD build worker nodes, batch data ingestion, small-scale caching layers, and web application serving.

Storage capabilities include a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume for rapid ephemeral disk I/O, while graphics acceleration is absent. Synthetic testing indicates moderate single-core performance with a stress-ng score of 1519.49 and a multi-core score of 3013.99, alongside 2.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.32 GB/sec static web throughput. The balanced combination of dedicated ARM cores and high-speed local NVMe storage makes this instance effective for lightweight web serving, build automation, small caching layers, and microservice workloads.
